reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across instances with XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both pattern recognition and model-level attribution are used to isolate features that are common, highly attributed, and semantically unrelated to the correct class.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify the exact feature(s) that are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 27244) and not present in correctly classified instances with similar demographics.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across all three misclassified instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate the semantic relevance of the shared features in the context of income prediction (e.g., marital status, occupation, education) and assess whether any of them are spurious or indirectly correlated via model bias.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A justified assessment of which shared features are semantically unrelated to the target class

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides global feature importance with interpretability, helping identify which features have high attribution across misclassified instances. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local explanations that can validate spurious importance in specific predictions. Sensitivity analysis isolates feature impact by ablation, revealing whether perturbing a shared feature alters predictions significantly—indicating spuriousness. Together, they ensure both shared presence and model-level attribution are examined for spuriousness.
